references.text: Describes the same phenomenon where many of the leaders (ἄρχοντες) believed in Jesus but did not confess it for fear of the Pharisaic leaders.
Introduces Nicodemus, a Pharisee and one of the leaders (ἄρχων), who comes to Jesus, showing that there were indeed believers among these groups.
Nicodemus and Joseph of Arimathea are shown here as leading (ἄρχοντες) disciples who only confessed their faith publicly after Jesus' death, illustrating the fear of expulsion mentioned in 7:48.
The chief priests and Pharisees gather in a council (synedrion), illustrating the political and religious power these groups held and why none of them dared to believe openly.
